text: Lesson 7's new index and Lesson 9's shorter transaction both work, today. But every insert, update, and delete against dbo dot Invoices after this point can still force page splits that gradually fragment IX_Invoices_PatientID, the same way any index degrades over time. A fix that isn't maintained is a fix with an expiration date nobody wrote down.

sys dot dm_db_index_physical_stats measures real fragmentation. Filtering to page_count greater than 500 matters as much as the fragmentation percentage itself — a small index at 80% fragmented isn't worth touching, because the whole thing fits in a handful of reads regardless of physical order.

Below 30% fragmented, REORGANIZE — lighter, always online. At or above 30%, REBUILD WITH ONLINE equals ON — thorough, heavier, but still non-blocking. This mirrors exactly the trade-off real DBA maintenance tooling makes automatically.

This decision script loops through every index over the page-count threshold and applies the right operation based on its own fragmentation level — not a blanket rule, but the real logic behind Ola Hallengren's widely-used Maintenance Solution, the community standard most shops install rather than reinventing from scratch.

Running this once fixes today's fragmentation and tells you nothing about next month's. IX_Invoices_PatientID will fragment again the moment real write traffic resumes — which is every single business day. This has to run on a schedule, which Lesson 11 sets up for real on Azure SQL Database.
